original_question: Determine the number N_k for each k, or improve the known bounds on N_k, where N_k bounds the dimensions in which geometrically k-orbit convex polytopes can exist.
target_in_paper: The draft is aiming at the geometric open problem in the paper’s discussion of k-orbit convex polytopes: after recalling Matteo’s theorem that for each k >= 2 there is a dimension threshold N_k beyond which no geometrically k-orbit convex d-polytopes exist, the paper asks whether the bounds on N_k can be improved and whether there are "holes" in the dimension spectrum for k-orbit polytopes.
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the main unknown quantity N_k, correctly ties it to geometrically k-orbit convex polytopes, and correctly frames the problem as either determining N_k exactly or improving existing bounds. This is very close to the paper’s intent.
missing_details: The paper’s quantifier is for each integer k >= 2.
N_k is tied to dimensions d of convex d-polytopes in Euclidean space, not abstract polytopes in general.
The relevant notion is geometrically k-orbit, meaning k flag-orbits under the Euclidean symmetry group, not combinatorially k-orbit under the full automorphism group.

To be stand-alone, the question should say explicitly that N_k is a threshold such that no geometrically k-orbit convex d-polytopes exist for d >= N_k; if one wants uniqueness, it is natural to ask for the least such threshold.
The nearby context includes the known exact values N_2 = 4, N_3 = 9, and N_4 = 8.

The paper’s official formulation also asks whether there are "holes" in the dimension spectrum, i.e. dimensions below N_k in which no geometrically k-orbit convex d-polytopes exist despite existence in other smaller dimensions.
Your draft does not make explicit that the problem is about existence by dimension, not classification of all such polytopes.
refined_question: For each integer k >= 2, let N_k be the least integer such that there exists no convex d-polytope in Euclidean space whose Euclidean symmetry group has exactly k orbits on flags whenever d >= N_k. Determine N_k for each k, or at least sharpen the known bounds on N_k; in addition, determine whether, for a fixed k, the set of dimensions d < N_k in which geometrically k-orbit convex d-polytopes exist can have gaps (that is, whether there are "holes" in the dimension spectrum).
justification: The draft is already close, but the paper’s actual target is narrower and slightly sharper. The surrounding discussion is not about arbitrary k-orbit abstract polytopes, but specifically about convex Euclidean d-polytopes that are geometrically k-orbit. The official formulation, as reflected in the geometric section of the paper and in the authors’ corresponding presentation of the same material, combines two linked questions: improving/determining the threshold N_k and understanding whether the admissible dimensions below that threshold form a contiguous set. Making N_k the least such threshold and spelling out the role of flag-orbits under the Euclidean symmetry group turns the draft into a stand-alone research question faithful to the paper.
